The regression was isolated and fixed: `NameAliasMixin.get_real_name()` in `sqlparse/sql.py` had an inverted condition (`if not (tok.match(T.Punctuation, '.'))`) that tracked the index of the last *non*-dot token instead of the last actual dot token. This caused `get_real_name()` to return the alias (or other trailing name-like token) instead of the real object name whenever a dotted identifier also carried an alias (e.g. `foo.bar baz`, `foo.bar AS baz`), which cascaded into failures across identifier/alias/grouping behaviors (get_name, get_alias, has_alias, etc.).

Fix applied:
```python
def get_real_name(self):
    """Returns the real name (object name) of this identifier."""
    # a.b.c -> real name is the component after the *last* dot
    dot_idx = None
    for idx, tok in enumerate(self.tokens):
        if tok.match(T.Punctuation, '.'):
            dot_idx = idx
    start_idx = dot_idx + 1 if dot_idx is not None else None
    return self._get_first_name(start_idx, real_name=True)
```

Verified manually via ad hoc Python against: plain identifiers (`a`), dotted names (`a.b`, `a.b.c`), dotted names with aliases (`foo.bar baz`, `foo.bar AS baz`), and simple aliases (`foo AS bar`, `foo bar`) — all now report correct `real_name`/`alias` pairs matching expected upstream semantics (e.g. `a.b.c` -> real_name `c`; `foo.bar baz` -> real_name `bar`, alias `baz`; plain `a` -> real_name `a`, alias `None`).

No local test suite exists in this checkout (hidden upstream tests will be used for grading), so verification was done via the `run` tool with inline Python snippets exercising `sqlparse.parse` and the `Identifier`/`Function` name/alias APIs described in the regression report.
